title: Greedy Best-First vs Bucharest Streets!
description: Watch Greedy Best-First race across a real street-map graph to find a route from start to goal. It chooses the next node using a heuristic estimate, often moving fast—but not always taking the optimal path.
ig_caption:
🗺️🚗 Routing on real streets in Bucharest (Sector 6)!

In this visualization, **Greedy Best-First** explores the graph nodes that look closest to the destination first. Under the hood, it prioritizes the frontier with an evaluation of **h(n)** (heuristic distance) and uses a priority queue to always expand the “most promising” intersection next. 📌

📐 **Graph theory lens:** we model intersections/road segments as a weighted graph (or grid-like graph) where each node is a location and edges represent reachable street connections. Greedy Best-First is a **best-first search** driven by the heuristic—meaning it may chase the lowest estimated distance and can overlook longer-but-better routes. 

⚙️ Want to see how far heuristics can push route quality? Drop a comment with your favorite heuristic (Manhattan, Euclidean, etc.) and I’ll compare runs! ✅
fb_caption:
🧠✨ Ever wonder how a computer “chooses streets” to reach a destination?

This reel visualizes **Greedy Best-First** as a graph search: intersections become nodes, streets become edges, and the algorithm uses a heuristic estimate to expand the most destination-close option first.
